18.description: Saskatoon will renew a five-year license agreement with Pattison Outdoor Advertising for six billboards at 140 Pacific Avenue, generating $33,000 annually for the property reserve.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
Revenue will be allocated to the property reserve to repay acquisition costs.

21.description: The committee recommends leasing a portion of Grace Adam Metawewinihk Park to Greater Saskatoon Catholic Schools for a secure outdoor area at St. Mary's Wellness and Education Centre, costing the city $8,000.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Councillor Donauer warned against setting a precedent for land deals with the province.
Public access to the existing playground and basketball court will remain.
Councillors worried the lease would set an unwanted precedent for land deals.
Which specific park project the $8,000 would be diverted from was unclear.
Vast majority of parents and community favored creating a fenced outdoor space.
School board anticipates fence installation will occur in early 2026.

23.description: The committee recommends City Council declare $26.7 million in profits from the Neighbourhood Land Development Fund, allocating $4 million to affordable housing and $20 million to major capital projects.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Councillors debated increasing affordable housing allocation from 15% to 25% for 2027.
Administration will report annually on the fund's status and major capital plan updates.

19.description: Saskatoon sold approximately $14.6 million in open market land and renewed several leases in 2025, with sales occurring in Ward 3 and the Parkridge neighborhood.

chips.text: Councillor Pierce expressed pleasure at land sales in Ward 3.

chips.text: Councillor Dunnauer highlighted strong management accountability and transparency ratings.
